# Primed SelectSeq admission

`oracle.json` contains compact classified results generated by the official
`dive-conformance golden generate` command against pinned TLC
`tlc-2026.10.06.014338` (upstream `94d0c5070852b37b801bb8998c436383ab7ee37b`).
It records the jar/JRE/classpath/library pins, source SHA-256 values, harness
source/binary identity and generation reason. The seed and fingerprint index
are both zero; TLC uses one worker and `-lncheck final`. No golden was edited.
Raw invocations and full generated goldens remain outside the repository.

To regenerate, stage these spec/config pairs as a separate external
Examples-layout corpus `primed-selectseq`, with one model directory per config.
Copy its named `.tla`, `.cfg`, `PayloadAbs.tla` and `SelectParam.tla` into each
directory and give its named spec/config an ordinary `manifest.json` entry.
Use the repository's pinned `oracles.toml` and a staging `corpora.toml` pointing
to that corpus. Run:

```sh
dive-conformance --repo-root "$STAGING" golden generate --corpus primed-selectseq --tier all --no-sany --reason 'Pin primed SelectSeq closure-isolation and demand-order regression controls' --workers 1 --jobs 2 --timeout 20 --xmx 1g --raw-invocations "$RAW"
```

The test consumes every classified case in `oracle.json`, comparing the verdict,
property, deciding class/code, physical TLC exit, counts and depth against the
reference, then checking the core at 1/4/8 workers in both profiles. It also
checks folding, eager aliases, memo/step-memo and hash-consing switches. These
are specifically selected controls, not a new whole-corpus agreement total.

| Cases | Boundary |
|---|---|
| `PureDirect`, `PureBindings` | Successor sequence changes; callback definition, configured operator, forwarded operator formal and LET definition remain pure. |
| `PureInstance` | EWD-shaped payload-message count substituted for an abstract state variable; refinement holds, 3 distinct / 4 generated / depth 3. |
| `PureBad` | Correct priming violates `Prop` on the first edge, 2112 / exit 13 / 2 distinct / 2 generated / depth 2. Its word validates independently; a forged successor is invalid. |
| `EmptyDemand`, `ShortCircuit` | An empty sequence never applies a failing callback; an earlier true disjunct never demands division by zero. |
| `SequenceErrorFirst`, `PredicateError` | Next-predicate evaluation reports the sequence's argument error 2169 before a failing callback, or the demanded callback's division-by-zero 2179, respectively. Both exit 255, with 1 distinct / 1 generated / depth 1. |
| `GlobalState`, `CapturedLocal`, `ConfiguredState`, `InstanceState`, `InstanceOpState` | Actual state reads and lexical captures remain refused after direct/configured/operator/INSTANCE resolution. Auto preserves reference results. |
| `EffectPrint`, `ConfiguredEffect` | Direct and configured callback printing remains refused; Auto retains reference output. |
| `OtherHigherOrder` | Primed `SortSeq` remains refused. |
| `FreePrime`, `DoublePrime` | Both frontends reject action-level prime arguments (SANY 4205, deciding 3002, exit 150). These are frontend controls, not evidence that the compiler's double-prime branch was reached. |
| `ConfiguredPrime` | A configured callback reaches a real primed state read in compilation and remains refused. The existing harness cannot classify TLC's action-property stream 2113/2121/2103 with exit 255, so it writes no golden. Only refusal and Auto/reference preservation are checked; no oracle agreement is claimed. |

The two Next-predicate error controls establish exact report/cause parity only.
Their final-expansion words retain the separate independent-successor proof
obligation (#434); they are not counted as independently validated errors.
Initial action-property forms exposing the existing unclassified oracle stream
were retained externally, without changing the harness's classification rules.

Independent source mutations are required to fail these tests: compiling the
sequence in plain mode, ignoring callback state reads, ignoring primed reads,
or allowing an unrelated free local. Runtime callback order and demand are
unchanged by this compiler-only admission. There are no new options or changed
TLC semantics.
